_meta.note: Hand-authored South Asian catalog: Mumbai, Delhi, Kolkata, Chennai, Bangalore and Hyderabad, with Karachi and Lahore. Shaped like Qloo Insights entities plus a `_syn` block used for scoring and stripped before serving. Entity ids are fake. Not Qloo data.

properties.short_description: The Nightingale of India: 'Aayega Aanewala', 'Ajeeb Dastan Hai Yeh', 'Lag Jaa Gale', the voice of a thousand films.
'Chaudhvin Ka Chand', 'Baharo Phool Barsao', 'Kya Hua Tera Wada': the voice behind Shammi Kapoor and Dilip Kumar.
'Roop Tera Mastana', 'Mere Sapno Ki Rani', 'Zindagi Ek Safar': the yodel and the laugh behind Rajesh Khanna.
'Awaara Hoon', 'Mera Joota Hai Japani', 'Kabhi Kabhie': the voice of Raj Kapoor.
'Dum Maro Dum', 'Piya Tu Ab To Aaja', 'Chura Liya': the sister with the cabaret voice, and the ghazals of Umrao Jaan.
'Waqt Ne Kiya Kya Haseen Sitam', 'Babuji Dheere Chalna': the voice of Guru Dutt's films.
'Poocho Na Kaise', 'Laga Chunari Mein Daag', 'Ae Meri Zohra Jabeen': the classically trained voice, and Bengali songs for Calcutta.
'Yeh Raat Yeh Chandni', 'Jaane Woh Kaise': the gentle baritone, and the Bengali 'Hemanta' of Rabindrasangeet.
The velvet voice of the ghazal: 'Jalte Hain Jiske Liye', 'Tasveer Teri Dil Mera'.
'Mere Desh Ki Dharti', 'Neele Gagan Ke Tale', 'Chalo Ek Baar Phir Se': the voice of Manoj Kumar's films.
Pancham: 'Dum Maro Dum', 'Chura Liya', 'Mehbooba Mehbooba'; the composer who made the seventies swing.
'Mere Sapno Ki Rani', 'Sar Jo Tera Chakraye', 'Wahan Kaun Hai Tera' in his own folk voice; the composer of Guide and Aradhana.
'Awaara Hoon', 'Yahoo!', 'Mera Joota Hai Japani': the composer duo of the Raj Kapoor and Shammi Kapoor years.
'Bindiya Chamkegi', 'Om Shanti Om', 'Mere Mehboob Qayamat Hogi': the duo who scored five hundred films.
'Tum Itna Jo Muskura Rahe Ho', 'Hothon Se Chhu Lo Tum': the ghazal in a baritone, with Chitra, from 1976.
Mallika-e-Ghazal: 'Aye Mohabbat Tere Anjaam Pe Rona Aaya', 'Woh Jo Hum Mein Tum Mein Qaraar Tha'.
The Carnatic voice of 'Kurai Onrum Illai' and the Suprabhatam at dawn; the first musician awarded the Bharat Ratna.
The Kirana gharana at full power; 'Mile Sur Mera Tumhara' opened with his voice.
The sitar that went to the world: Monterey, Woodstock, the Concert for Bangladesh, and George Harrison's teacher.
The shehnai of Varanasi, played at the Red Fort on the first Independence Day.
The voice of MGR and Sivaji Ganesan: 'Paattum Naane', 'Naan Aanaiyittal', the Tamil screen from the 1950s on.
The Tamil and Telugu playback queen: 'Paal Vannam Paruvam', 'Ninnu Kori' and thousands more.
The voice of Telugu cinema: 'Siva Sankari', the Bhagavad Gita, every NTR song of the fifties and sixties.
'Gaana Gandharvan': Malayalam, Tamil and Hindi, 'Chand Jaise Mukhde Pe', 'Harivarasanam'.
SPB: 'Sankarabharanam', 'Ilaya Nila', 'Tere Mere Beech Mein'; forty thousand songs in sixteen languages from 1966.
The Maestro: from Annakili (1976), the strings and the folk of the Tamil countryside.
The bard of the Brahmaputra: 'Bistirno Parore', 'Dil Hoom Hoom Kare'.
Shahenshah-e-Ghazal: 'Ranjish Hi Sahi', 'Gulon Mein Rang Bhare', from Radio Pakistan to the world.
Malika-e-Tarannum: 'Awaz De Kahan Hai' in Bombay, then the voice of Pakistani cinema and the 1965 war songs.
Shahenshah-e-Qawwali: 'Allah Hoo', 'Tumhe Dillagi', from the dargahs to Peter Gabriel.

properties.description: K. Asif's Anarkali and Salim; 'Pyar Kiya To Darna Kya' in the Sheesh Mahal.
Nargis as Radha, the mother who ploughs the field and shoots her son.
Guru Dutt's poet nobody will publish; 'Jaane Woh Kaise' and the Calcutta streets.
Raj Kapoor's tramp in Bombay; 'Mera Joota Hai Japani' and the umbrella in the rain.
Dev Anand and Waheeda Rehman; 'Aaj Phir Jeene Ki Tamanna Hai' and the S. D. Burman score.
Raj Kapoor's love triangle in Technicolor, with Europe for the honeymoon.
Shammi Kapoor's drummer and the murder in the hill station; 'O Haseena Zulfonwali'.
Dev Anand as the man mistaken for a thief; 'Hothon Pe Aisi Baat' on the giant drum.
Kishore Kumar, Mehmood and Sunil Dutt in the funniest musical duel in Hindi film.
Rajesh Khanna and Sharmila Tagore in the toy train; 'Mere Sapno Ki Rani' and the start of superstardom.
Rajesh Khanna's dying man who refuses to be sad; 'Babumoshai, zindagi badi honi chahiye, lambi nahin.'
Meena Kumari's courtesan, fourteen years in the making; 'Chalte Chalte' and 'Inhi Logon Ne'.
Rajesh Khanna and Sharmila Tagore on the Hooghly; 'Chingari Koi Bhadke', 'Pushpa, I hate tears.'
Rishi Kapoor and Dimple Kapadia, sixteen and in love; 'Main Shayar To Nahin'.
Jai and Veeru against Gabbar Singh in Ramgarh; the film that ran five years at Minerva.
Amitabh Bachchan's angry young man and the brother with the badge; 'Mere paas maa hai.'
Hrishikesh Mukherjee's professor pretending to be a driver who speaks only pure Hindi.
Yash Chopra's poets and lovers across two generations; 'Kabhi Kabhie Mere Dil Mein' in Mukesh's voice.
Three brothers, three faiths, one blood transfusion; Manmohan Desai's masala at full tilt.
The devotional sleeper hit of 1975 that filled cinemas with women and prayer.
Yash Chopra's lost-and-found family in Technicolor; 'Ae Meri Zohra Jabeen'.
Rajesh Khanna and his four elephants; 'Chal Chal Chal Mere Haathi'.
Satyajit Ray's Apu and Durga in the paddy fields, the train and the rain; Ravi Shankar's sitar.
Ray's lonely wife on the swing, Madhabi Mukherjee and the opera glasses.
Uttam Kumar and Suchitra Sen in the Bengali romance; 'Ei Path Jodi Na Shesh Hoy' on the motorbike.
Sivaji Ganesan's debut and the courtroom speech that shook Madras.
MGR's double role as the king and the vagabond, half in Gevacolor.
Sivaji Ganesan's Kattabomman thunders at the Company's collector.
MGR's double role, the whip and 'Naan Aanaiyittal'.
Sivaji's nadaswaram player and Padmini's dancer; the music of Thanjavur in Eastmancolor.
MGR goes around the world, Hong Kong to Tokyo, in the biggest Tamil hit of the seventies.
NTR as Krishna, SVR as Ghatotkacha and the laddoos; the Telugu film everyone can quote.
K. Viswanath's classical singer and the devadasi's daughter; SPB's Carnatic score.
Rajkumar's golden man of the Kannada village, two years in the Bangalore cinemas.
Pakistan's Waheed Murad and Zeba, 'Akele Na Jana' and 'Ko Ko Korina'; the first Pakistani film to run 75 weeks.
Firdous and Ejaz in Masud Pervaiz's Punjabi epic of the lovers.
Half an hour of film songs on Doordarshan, Wednesdays and Fridays, the whole mohalla watching.
Doordarshan's first soap: the Ram family, Basesar's drinking, and Ashok Kumar's closing word.
Ramesh Sippy's Partition family saga, Master Haveli Ram and Lajoji.
Ramanand Sagar's Sunday mornings, when the streets emptied and the TV sets were garlanded.
B. R. Chopra's epic, 'Main samay hoon', every Sunday after Ramayan.
R. K. Narayan's Swami and his friends, Shankar Nag's gentle Malgudi.
Doordarshan's programme for farmers, the longest-running on Indian television.
Tabassum's film-star chat show on Doordarshan, one of its first.
Shafi Inamdar and Swaroop Sampat's sitcom, with Satish Shah in a new role every week.
Saeed Mirza's street corner: Khopdi, Guru and the chai stall.
R. K. Laxman's common man, Anjan Srivastav as Srinivas Wagle.
Shah Rukh Khan's first role, as Abhimanyu Rai in commando training.
Madras Doordarshan's Friday-night film songs, Tamil Nadu's Chitrahaar.
PTV's sketch comedy with Bushra Ansari and Ismail Tara.
PTV's serial of Shaukat Siddiqui's novel, the Karachi slum and its people.
PTV's feudal saga of Chaudhry Hashmat and his sons; the streets of Lahore emptied for it.
The Colaba Causeway café since 1871, beer towers and the traveller's Bombay.
Berry pulao at the Parsi café of 1923 in Ballard Estate, Boman Kohinoor at the table.
properties.address: Wakefield House, Sprott Road, Ballard Estate, Mumbai

properties.description: Bun maska and Irani chai at Marine Lines since 1904, the oldest Irani café in the city.
Mario Miranda's murals and the jukebox, in Colaba since 1932.
The Churchgate restaurant of 1956, the film crowd's lunch and the pastry counter.
Seekh kebabs off the pavement behind the Taj since 1946, open past midnight.
Bhel, pani puri and kulfi on the sand at Girgaum Chowpatty, the evening out of a lifetime.
The Gujarati thali of Kalbadevi since 1945, unlimited and unhurried.
The Fort restaurant of 1958 with its Husain and Anjolie Ela Menon on the walls, raan and rogan josh.
properties.address: 145 M. G. Road, Kala Ghoda, Mumbai

properties.description: Mughlai kebabs and korma in the lane by Jama Masjid since 1913, the cooks' lineage from the royal kitchen.
Where butter chicken and tandoori chicken were born, Daryaganj, 1947; Nehru's regular table.
Chhole bhature and ice cream at the Regal Building restaurant since 1940.
The grand Connaught Place coffee house of 1942, chandeliers and the mutton cutlet.
properties.address: E-15 Inner Circle, Connaught Place, Delhi

properties.description: The cooperative coffee house of 1957: turbaned waiters, filter coffee, and the arguments of a nation.
properties.address: Mohan Singh Place, Baba Kharak Singh Marg, Delhi

properties.description: The lane of stuffed paranthas in Chandni Chowk, fried since the 1870s.
properties.address: Paranthe Wali Gali, Chandni Chowk, Delhi

properties.description: The Connaught Place hotel of 1934 that became the first fast-food and ice-cream chain of Delhi, hot chocolate fudge and all.
The sweet shop of Chandni Chowk since 1790, sohan halwa for the emperors.
The Park Street tea room of 1927: rum balls, the English breakfast and the pink façade.
The adda of adda: Satyajit Ray, Amartya Sen and every student with a cup of coffee and a cigarette.
properties.address: 15 Bankim Chatterjee Street, College Street, Kolkata

properties.description: The Park Street restaurant of 1956: chicken à la Kiev, devilled crab and the red leather booths.
The kathi roll was invented here, New Market, 1932.
Park Street's live-music restaurant of 1939, where Usha Uthup sang in the sixties.
The rosogolla in a tin, the sweet shop of the Das family on Esplanade since the 1930s.
The Jewish bakery in New Market since 1902, fruit cake and cheese samosas.
Chicken 65 was invented here in 1965, the Mount Road restaurant of 1951.
Idli drowned in sambar at Triplicane since 1948.
Dosas served to the car window under the trees of Cathedral Road, 1962 to 2008.
The K. K. Nagar original of 1981 that became the world's South Indian restaurant.
Madurai's idlis and podi, in Chennai since the 1990s but on every tongue since.
Mavalli Tiffin Rooms, the rava idli's birthplace, Lalbagh Road since 1924.
The Basavanagudi masala dosa since 1943, the waiter with twelve plates up his arm.
The St. Mark's Road restaurant of 1940, Parade Café, mutton cutlets and the city's arguments.
The Secunderabad café of 1953 that became the biryani of Hyderabad.
Dum biryani at Basheerbagh since 1973.
Fruit biscuits and dil kush from the Mozamjahi Market bakery of 1953.
The kebabs of Karachi since 1948, on M. A. Jinnah Road.
The Saddar biryani stand of 1969 that became a chain.
The Mall's literary café since 1940, Faiz and Manto at the tables.
Trotters and head at dawn by Lohari Gate, since 1958.
The arch of 1924 on the harbour, the boats to Elephanta and the Taj behind it.
The Queen's Necklace, the evening walk along the sea wall with the lights coming on.
Pav bhaji on the sand and the film stars' bungalows behind the palms.
The terraced gardens on Malabar Hill and the boot house, the sunset over Chowpatty.
The Gothic railway cathedral of 1887, now Chhatrapati Shivaji Terminus.
The art-deco cinema of 1938 opposite Churchgate station.
Colaba's art-deco picture house of 1933, the first air-conditioned cinema in India.
The MGM art-deco palace of 1938 at Dhobi Talao.
properties.address: M. G. Road, Dhobi Talao, Mumbai

properties.description: The fruit and bird market of 1869 under the clock tower, Kipling's father's friezes on the gate.
The white shrine on the causeway into the sea, reached at low tide.
The Ganesha temple at Prabhadevi, Tuesday queues around the block.
properties.address: S. K. Bole Marg, Prabhadevi, Mumbai

properties.description: The Cricket Club of India's ground of 1937, Test matches with the sea breeze.
The Dadar maidan of cricket nets and political rallies.
Kala Ghoda's gallery of 1952 and the Samovar café in its corridor.
properties.address: 161B M. G. Road, Kala Ghoda, Mumbai

properties.description: The war memorial arch of 1931 at the end of Rajpath, ice cream on the lawns at night.
Shah Jahan's fort of 1648, the flag on Independence Day and the Sound and Light show.
properties.address: Netaji Subhash Marg, Chandni Chowk, Delhi

properties.description: The 73-metre minaret of 1193 in Mehrauli, the picnic ground of Delhi.
The white colonnades of 1933: the Regal and Odeon cinemas, Wenger's and the Madras Coffee House.
The great mosque of 1656 above Chandni Chowk, the Eid crowds on its steps.
properties.address: Jama Masjid Road, Chandni Chowk, Delhi

properties.description: Tombs of the Lodis among the lawns, the morning walk of New Delhi.
The old city's bazaar from the Red Fort to Fatehpuri, jalebis, saris and the Gurudwara Sis Ganj.
The red sandstone and marble garden tomb of 1572, the Taj Mahal's model.
The National Zoological Park of 1959 beside the Old Fort, the white tigers.
The exhibition grounds of 1972, the Trade Fair every November and the Hall of Nations.
The Laxminarayan Temple of 1939, opened by Gandhi on condition that all castes could enter.
Delhi's cricket ground since 1883, in the ruins of the old fort.
The white marble memorial of 1921 on the Maidan, the gardens and the evening promenade.
The cantilever bridge of 1943 over the Hooghly, the busiest in the world.
The cricket ground of 1864, a hundred thousand voices in the stands.
The great green of the city: football, cricket, the Victoria Memorial and the tram lines across it.
The Kali temple of 1809 that gave the city its name.
The temple of 1855 on the Hooghly, Ramakrishna's temple.
The street of restaurants, Christmas lights and the Park Street jazz of the sixties.
Sir Stuart Hogg Market of 1874, the clock tower and everything under one roof.
The oldest zoo in India, 1876; the winter picnic of Calcutta.
The oldest museum in India, 1814, the Egyptian mummy and the Bharhut gateway.
The MGM art-deco cinema of 1935 on Chowringhee.
The planetarium of 1963 on Chowringhee, every school trip of the city.
The longest urban beach in the country, sundal and the evening crowds.
The Mylapore temple with the painted gopuram, the Arupathimoovar festival.
The East India Company's fort of 1644, St Mary's Church and the museum.
The Mount Road department store of 1863, the Indo-Saracenic building that burned in 1983.
The red-brick market of 1898 by Central station, second-hand books and pets, lost to fire in 1985.
The oldest bookshop in India, on Mount Road since 1844.
The December music season since 1928, the Carnatic kutcheri and the canteen.
The cricket ground of 1916, the tied Test of 1986.
The stone chariot of 1976 to the poet Thiruvalluvar.
Tipu's garden of 1760 and the Glass House, the flower show every January and August.
The green lung of 1870 in the middle of the city, the red library and the bandstand.
Mahatma Gandhi Road and Brigade Road: Plaza cinema, Koshy's and the evening walk.
The Tudor-style palace of 1878 on the Wodeyars' estate.
The four minarets of 1591 in the heart of the old city, bangles in the Laad Bazaar around it.
The lake of 1563 between the twin cities, Tank Bund and the evening boats.
The diamond kings' fort, the clap at the gate heard at the top.
One man's collection of 1951: the Veiled Rebecca and the musical clock at noon.
Camel rides and the Abdullah Shah Ghazi shrine above the sand.
Jinnah's white marble mausoleum of 1970 in its gardens.
The Saddar market of 1889 under its clock tower.
Aurangzeb's red sandstone mosque of 1673, across from the fort.
The oldest bazaar in the city, saris, shoes and the food street.
Shah Jahan's terraced gardens of 1641 and their four hundred fountains.
The summer capital on the Ridge, the Mall and the toy train from Kalka.
Tea gardens, Tiger Hill at dawn and the toy train; the Calcutta family's hill station.
The Nilgiris' Snooty Ooty: the lake, the botanical gardens and the Blue Mountain train.
Dal Lake houseboats, shikaras and the Mughal gardens; the honeymoon of a generation.
The beaches, the churches and the feni, from Bombay by boat or the Konkan road.
Strawberries, Venna Lake and the viewpoints of the Bombay family's hill station.
Chikki, the monsoon waterfalls and the ghats between Bombay and Poona.
The car-free hill station, the toy train and the horses.
The Taj Mahal by moonlight, the fort and the petha.
The ghats at dawn, the Ganga aarti and the lanes of Kashi.
The Jagannath temple, the Rath Yatra and the Bengali family's seaside.
Calcutta's own seaside, the casuarina trees and the long low tide.
The lake in the Kumaon hills, boats and the Naina Devi temple.
The Queen of the Hills, the Mall, Kempty Falls and the Doon below.
The star-shaped lake in the Palani hills, the Princess of Hill Stations.
The seven hills of Tirumala and the laddu, the busiest pilgrimage in the world.
Har Ki Pauri and the evening aarti where the Ganga leaves the hills.
Rajasthan's only hill station: Nakki Lake and the Dilwara temples.
The pink city, Hawa Mahal and the elephants up to Amber.
The palace lit up at Dasara, Chamundi Hill and the Brindavan Gardens fountains.
The Mall and the pines above Rawalpindi, the hill station of Pakistan.
The Switzerland of the East: the valley, the river and Kalam.
